blocks.note: The market adds USD 2.6 Bn by 2033 on recurring, regulation-driven testing.
blocks.text: Global blood bank serology revenue rises from **USD 3,329.28 Mn** in 2025 to **USD 5,893.08 Mn** by 2033, adding **USD 2,563.8 Mn**. Growth rests on mandatory donor screening and pre-transfusion compatibility testing rather than discretionary demand.

blocks.note: Immunoassay, hospital transfusion labs and North America hold the largest pools of new revenue.
blocks.text: The largest new revenue pools are **immunoassay** (+USD 854.0 Mn), **hospital-based transfusion labs** (+USD 1,084.4 Mn) and **North America** (+USD 986.6 Mn). The fastest growth is in **gel / column agglutination** (8.28%), **plasma fractionation labs** (8.09%), **anti-HBc** screening (8.85%) and **Asia Pacific** (8.08%).

blocks.note: Share is won country by country; six suppliers hold 57.9% globally.
blocks.text: Six suppliers hold **57.9%** of global revenue, led by **QuidelOrtho** (17.9%), but leadership changes by country. Regulatory approvals and clearances make up **58.6%** of tracked developments.

items.a: Hospital transfusion labs (+USD 1,084.4 Mn), immunoassay (+USD 854.0 Mn), immunohematology serology (+USD 1,494.5 Mn) and North America (+USD 986.6 Mn).
Segments that are both large in new revenue and fast-growing: immunoassay, gel / column agglutination, plasma fractionation labs, solid-phase, reference labs, anti-HBc and antibody identification.
Uneven infrastructure, regulatory fragmentation and reagent supply continuity, plus country-by-country competitive leadership.

blocks.text: Market sizes and CAGRs are taken from the GVR report. Incremental revenue is the 2033 value minus the 2025 value. Each segment is placed in one of four priority groups using two thresholds: incremental revenue of at least USD 200 Mn, and a CAGR of at least 7.5%, close to the market rate of 7.45%.

blocks.text: Revenue grew from USD 2,577.87 Mn in 2021 to USD 3,329.28 Mn in 2025 and is forecast to reach USD 5,893.08 Mn by 2033, a CAGR of 7.45% over 2026–2033. Growth accelerates in absolute terms each year, from USD 233.9 Mn in 2026 to USD 431.7 Mn in 2033 (calculated).
Product and testing area are two views of the same total. Software and services grow fastest (9.17%) from the smallest base; reagents and consumables add the most revenue (USD 1,568.4 Mn).

items.text: Resource-limited blood services stay manual or semi-automated; advanced systems concentrate in reference labs.
Assay classification, validation and marker panels differ by country, multiplying technical files and registrations.
Shelf life, cold chain, batch acceptance testing and stock rotation shape purchasing beyond price.

blocks.text: The opportunity is broad but concentrated: three pools account for most of the new revenue, and the fastest growth sits in automation and plasma testing.
